summary.headline: Rentomojo Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose about 53% YoY to a stated base, with normalized EBITDA of ~58.8 crore and CFO near 110% of EBITDA.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up about 53% YoY and 12.5% QoQ, with normalized EBITDA of about 58.8 crore (vs 38.5 crore in Q2 FY26) and normalized PAT of about 24 crore (vs 15.8 crore). Reported PAT was distorted by a roughly 6 crore deferred tax asset charge and one-time items (gratuity/leave reversal of about 1.2 crore gain, IPO expense of about 80 lakh). Operating volumes grew strongly: gross items ordered up about 45% YoY and subscribers up about 42.5% YoY, with occupancy at 86%. Management reiterated that operating cash flow tracks EBITDA at roughly 110%, and that capex is now being funded mainly from accruals, with debt second in the funding waterfall.

segments.name: Subscription rental (furniture and appliances)
segments.commentary: Gross items ordered about 3.8 lakh in Q2 (+45% YoY, +16% QoQ); about 710,000 items in H1 equivalent to about 860 crore purchase displacement. Live subscribers +42.5% YoY, live items +44% YoY, items per user stable at about 2.8, occupancy about 86% (up from 83%).

segments.name: Water purifiers and air purifiers
segments.commentary: Water purifiers a small base but growing fast; management says it does not sell these items to avoid cannibalising rental revenue. Air purifiers already on platform.

segments.name: Experience stores
segments.commentary: Seven stores added in Q2, mainly in Delhi, Mumbai and Pune; store count up about 43% YoY over the period cited. About 90-91% of growth still from core cities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT expectation of about 90-95 crore reiterated; management said item-per-user growth is not baked into this.
Capex run-rate: H1 FY27 capex of about 170-175 crore, implying roughly double for full year per management.
Revenue growth trajectory cited as 35%-38%, 40%, 45%, 50%, 52-53% over recent quarters; management said it is aiming for growth well above the 30-35% industry-talk level.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around 40-41%, with room to absorb higher customer acquisition costs by curtailing experience investments.
Revenue per item may dip in H2 due to AC seasonality (higher-capex items deployed in H1); management expects normalization on an annualized basis.
Management targets return on capital above 25% and aspires to ROE/ROCE of 20% and above; net debt to equity tolerance discussed up to about 1x.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about 170-175 crore (management stated range); H1 gross capex about 192.3 crore including warehouse capex and scrapped items.
Gross fixed asset base rose from about 530 crore to about 703 crore in H1; net fixed assets from 426 crore to 566 crore.
Warehouse square feet capacity up about 51% YoY; store count up about 43% YoY.
AC capex per item about three to four times normal per-item capex, concentrated in April to June/July.
Capex funded mainly from accruals (H1 CFO about 110 crore); external debt second in funding waterfall, free cash flow focus expected in a few years.
demand_pricing: Revenue per item up about 4.6% YoY in Q2 and about 6% on an H1 basis; management said it is not banking on this for targets.
Implied value per item rose to about 11,700 in Q2 FY27 from about 10,600 in Q2 FY26, attributed to mix (ACs, sofas, higher-capex categories).
Traffic up about 50% YoY; Rentomojo keyword search up about 66% YoY; industry keyword growth about 20-25%.

Industry penetration: rental about 1% of furniture and 1.4% of appliance purchase volume (about 2,000 crore by value, per analyst). Management cites about 3.8 crore addressable apartments (about 4.8 crore total), and says the industry has served only about 15-20 lakh households so far.
Management says the organized market is largely a duopoly; marketing and advertising as a share of revenue has risen over recent quarters but remains within target limits.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational capex be funded given the growth runway?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accruals will fund most capex now, debt is the second source within debt-to-equity constraints (net debt to equity 0.28x), and free cash flow focus comes in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue per item grow significantly or linearly?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue per item grew about 6% on an H1-to-H1 basis; management is not setting targets on it and expects a possible H2 dip from AC seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic, category and channel mix of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is broad-based across core categories with some new ones like water purifiers; core cities remain the main focus, with about 90-91% of growth from them. Channel-level split was offered offline.

qa_highlights.question: Items per user: capped at 2.8 or can it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Items per user rose from 2.3 to 2.8 historically; management is not baking further growth into FY27 PBT guidance of about 90-95 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Debt capacity, cost of debt and net debt to equity comfort?
qa_highlights.answer: Latest debt raised at about 8.65%, all long-term, from large public and private banks; CRISIL rating review under way. Management said comfort could extend toward about 1x net debt to equity for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H2 historically more profitable and cash generative?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said costs are linked to items deployed, which is heavier in H1; H2 deploys fewer items while earlier items keep generating revenue at no incremental cost.

qa_highlights.question: Status of NCLT matters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined detail as matter is sub judice; a hearing is scheduled for December.

risks_watch: Reported vs normalized gap: Q1 fire loss (about 11.4 crore PAT impact), recurring deferred tax asset charges, and exceptional items; watch whether reported PAT converges with normalized.
Revenue per item may dip in H2 with AC seasonality; item per user growth is not in guidance.
Customer acquisition cost may rise with new cities and channels; marketing spend share of revenue has increased.
NCLT proceedings pending with a December hearing; management declined to comment in detail.
Rising interest rate environment; management says cost of debt sensitivity is lower than occupancy or useful life.
Net debt to equity and capex pace: capex growing faster than revenue; monitor funding mix as debt rises.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capital efficiency and cash conversion, with repeated emphasis on normalized numbers. Evasive on NCLT matters (sub judice), on forward item-per-user and revenue-per-item assumptions, and on H2 specifics beyond historical patterns.
key_quotes: If you look at our contractual revenue tied in at the end of Quarter 2, it actually stood at close to about 690 odd crores.
Frankly, this is a negative working capital business, and that's why you're seeing almost around 110 odd% translation from EBITDA into cash flow.
Occupancy at 85% is more important than possibly a cost of financing at 8.65% versus 9.6% versus 10%.
We don't sell. We don't want dual revenues coming in which are cannibalistic in nature, so we're not selling for sure.
There is a hearing in December that will happen, but since the matter is completely sub judice, I don't want to talk more than what we have already disclosed in the prospectus
